project.name: Python automation exercises
project.summary: Independent learning scripts for terminal input, collections, text formatting and clipboard operations. There is no shared server, persisted database or application-wide pipeline.

nodes.label: Prompt and number exercises
nodes.summary: Small standalone scripts teach input loops, guesses, validation and arithmetic.

nodes.label: Text, grids and tables
nodes.summary: Standalone examples count characters, join lists and align or transpose printed rows.

nodes.label: Inventory and board games
nodes.summary: Examples mutate in-memory dictionaries, alternate board turns and choose a random message.

nodes.label: Clipboard and variable scope
nodes.summary: Clipboard scripts use pyperclip; separate scope demonstrations contrast global/local bindings.

nodes.label: Terminal input and output
nodes.summary: Each chosen script starts independently and reads or prints through the terminal.

nodes.label: Operating-system clipboard
nodes.summary: pyperclip reads or replaces clipboard text; no clipboard contents are bundled.

edges.label: Enter requested values
edges.description: The selected exercise consumes input; these scripts do not call one another.

edges.label: Print a result or another prompt
edges.description: Loops may repeat, terminate, or reject invalid input according to the chosen script.

edges.label: Choose an account argument
edges.description: pw.py looks up the supplied account in its in-memory dictionary.

edges.label: Replace clipboard text
edges.description: pw.py copies a stored value; bulletPointAdder.py copies bullet-prefixed lines.

edges.label: Read clipboard lines
edges.description: Only bulletPointAdder.py reads the existing clipboard.

edges.label: Print formatted examples
edges.description: Each text script uses its own embedded demonstration input.

edges.label: Show inventory or board
edges.description: The inventory and board examples print in-memory state, not saved records.

steps.note: Start collatz.py and enter an integer.
Repeatedly divide an even number by two or multiply an odd number by three and add one, printing each step until one. A conversion ValueError prints a message; it does not reprompt.
Read the sequence. Nonpositive inputs have no guaranteed termination in this exercise.
Provide text already on the clipboard.
bulletPointAdder.py splits on newline, prefixes every line with an asterisk and space, then rejoins the lines.
Replace the clipboard with the transformed text; no file is saved.

tour.title: Choose one script at a time
tour.note: This repository is a set of learning exercises, not interconnected services. Birthdays exist only in one process dictionary.

tour.title: Formatting has explicit examples
tour.note: Both table printers transpose equal-length lists into right-aligned columns; the grid example prints columns as rows.

tour.title: Board turns are not game validation
tour.note: ticTacToe.py accepts a dictionary key and alternates nine moves without a winner check or occupied-square protection.

tour.title: Not a secure password manager
tour.note: pw.py stores credentials in source and copies them to the clipboard. Its add branch changes only memory and does not copy the newly entered value. The map uses an exact-literal-redacted derivative.

tour.title: Some exercises intentionally fail
tour.note: sameName4.py reads a local variable before assignment. The map documents the code; it does not claim all scripts execute successfully.
